items.label: Max RAM (128 MB min); up to 6 vCPUs

items.name: Concurrency
items.text: Shared unreserved pool; 429 sync vs 6h async retry. SQS uses max concurrency; Kinesis/DDB Streams scale by shards × parallelization.

items.name: When NOT to use
items.tag: AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Step Functions
items.text: Skip for >15 min runs, >10 GB RAM/GPUs, GB–TB joins, steady high-throughput (use EMR/ECS), or sync chaining (use Step Functions).

items: Set memory, not CPU: CPU & network scale with memory, so higher RAM often runs faster and cheaper.
EFS requires a VPC; add VPC endpoints or a NAT gateway if Lambda also calls S3 or AWS APIs.
Reserved concurrency guarantees & caps capacity; provisioned concurrency removes cold starts.
DLQ/on-failure dest is async-only (streams use ESM dest). Put heavy libs in layers or container images.

blocks.caption: Reserved = guarantee + cap (free); Provisioned = warm instances for low latency (paid).
blocks.heading: Reserved vs provisioned concurrency

points: Guarantees capacity up to N from account pool
Caps max concurrency at N to protect downstream DBs
Setting reserved concurrency to 0 pauses the function
